details.body: Add a comment to the `system:habitat_registry_finalize` stage in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs` (around line 376-382) explaining WHY a second refresh is needed: `update_daily_filter_clogging` modifies `filter_state.clogging_index`, which `compute_filter_media` reads (habitat.rs:164) to compute FilterMedia oxygen exposure. Without this comment, the dual-refresh pattern looks redundant and a future contributor may remove it, silently introducing stale clogging data in the serialized registry.

In `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs` line 727, the unconditional `self.state.refresh_habitat_registry()` at the end of `process_action` runs after every player action including `Feed`, `AddShrimp`, `RemoveShrimp`, and `SiphonDetritus`, none of which modify habitat-relevant state (geometry, hardware, plants, substrate, or filter). Consider either (a) making the refresh conditional on action type, or (b) adding a brief comment explaining that the unconditional approach is an intentional simplicity-over-performance trade-off. This prevents future confusion about whether the unconditional call is deliberate or an oversight.

Rework substrate habitat area calculation so it depends on the actual substrate amount, not stored constants. Right now `SubstrateSurface` only checks whether `substrate_layers` is empty and otherwise returns the full footprint (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:205-209`), while `SubstrateDeep` just sums the serialized `layer.colonizable_area_cm2` values (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:220-225`). Those per-layer areas are precomputed as `footprint * colonizable_area_factor` without any depth term in scenario materialization (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:748-754`), and the default layer hardcodes `100.0 cm²` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:24-33`). The result is that larger tanks, deeper layers, or zero-depth layers can report the wrong substrate habitat area even after `refresh_habitat_registry()`.

Derive plant crowding inside the habitat registry refresh path, or recompute `PlantGuildState.crowding_index` before every registry rebuild. `compute_habitat_registry()` attenuates habitat light from the cached `crowding_index` field (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:85-94`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:179`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:199`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:215`), but scenario materialization seeds every plant with a placeholder `crowding_index: 0.1` regardless of biomass or tank size (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:783-788`), and trim actions change biomass then immediately refresh the registry without recalculating crowding (`crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:628-649`, `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:727`). That leaves `GlassHardscape`, `PlantSurfaces`, and `SubstrateSurface` light exposure stale after startup and after biomass-changing actions until the next daily plant-growth pass.

Use the actual water column above the substrate when computing `SubstrateSurface.light_exposure`. The current attenuation term is based on `state.geometry.mean_depth_cm()` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:117`), but `mean_depth_cm()` is just `fill_height_cm` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:60-61`), so changing substrate depth does not change substrate-surface light even though the habitat surface moves closer to or farther from the lamp. `TankState::substrate_depth_cm()` already exists (`crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:172-177`) and could be used to derive the real water depth above the substrate.

In `SubstrateLayerState::default()` (substrate.rs:56), `colonizable_area_cm2` is hardcoded to `100.0`, but the derived value for default geometry (40×25cm, InertSand, 3cm depth) is `1500.0` — a 15× discrepancy. While `refresh_habitat_registry()` always overwrites this, any code that constructs substrate layers via `..Default::default()` and reads `colonizable_area_cm2` before engine initialization will silently get a wrong value. Fix: compute the default via `Self::derived_colonizable_area_cm2` using `TankGeometry::default().footprint_area_cm2()`, or replace the field default with `0.0` and document it as derived-only to make stale reads immediately obvious.

`crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:798-803` hard-codes hours `0..7` as the lit window for the 8-hour photoperiod, but `crates/tank_core/src/systems/light.rs:9-13` centers the photoperiod on noon, and its own unit test at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/light.rs:21-23` shows the actual lit hours are `8..15`. As written, `do_dips_at_night_in_planted_tank` is comparing the wrong samples and currently fails on the checked-in tree. That test should derive lit/dark buckets from `is_light_on(...)` instead of assuming midnight-start lighting.

`SubstratePreset` exposes a configurable `colonizable_area_factor` in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:223-233`, but that factor is never carried into serialized engine state. `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:733-761` reduces presets to `SubstrateKind`, and every later recomputation in `crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:11-23` and `crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:241-244` uses hard-coded per-kind factors instead. That means any future preset tweak or custom substrate data will be silently discarded the next time `refresh_habitat_registry()` runs, leaving the habitat registry with a second, divergent source of truth for substrate area.

In `affects_habitat_registry()` (actions.rs:159-169), `ChangePhotoperiod` is listed as affecting the habitat registry, but the habitat computation in `compute_habitat_registry` reads `hardware.light.intensity_index` not `hardware.light.photoperiod_hours`. Photoperiod changes produce a redundant registry refresh. Either remove `ChangePhotoperiod` from the match, or add a code comment explaining the deliberate over-approximation so future maintainers don't second-guess it.

The legacy `total_colonizable_area_cm2()` (biology.rs:660-669) used by `algae_growth.rs:167` computes colonizable area as `wall_area_cm2 + substrate_layers.colonizable_area_cm2`, which omits `geometry.hardscape_area_cm2`. Now that hardscape area is a configurable field on `TankGeometry`, adding hardscape to a tank increases habitat registry `GlassHardscape` area but the algae carrying-capacity model ignores it entirely. Add a note (doc comment or inline TODO) clarifying this omission so the downstream habitatization task (tanksim-6e5.5.3) knows to migrate algae to the habitat registry rather than the legacy helper.

Context:
- The current simulation tracks a tank, substrate, and filter, but not a general habitat model for surfaces and zones.
- To make biofilms, periphyton, redox, and geometry matter for the right reasons, the engine needs a first-class habitat registry.

- Define a compact habitat registry in engine state/save data covering at least filter media, glass/hardscape, plant surfaces, substrate surface, and deeper substrate.

- Make the modifiers responsive to relevant scenario inputs where appropriate (for example filter flow, depth/light context, rooted plant presence) while keeping the model ecological rather than graphical.
- Keep the abstraction small and inspectable so later habitatized systems can build on it without redesigning state yet again.

  GlassHardscape
  PlantSurfaces
  SubstrateSurface
  SubstrateDeep

## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance Criteria:
- habitats are explicit serialized engine concepts with documented purpose and minimal required metadata.
- colonizable areas are derived from geometry, hardware, and plant state rather than hardcoded constants, and plant-driven areas update when biomass changes.
- flow, oxygen, and light exposure modifiers are documented, bounded in [0,1], and respond to the relevant scenario inputs for each habitat.
- representative tests cover registry serialization, area computation, and modifier sensitivity/bounds so later habitatized systems can build on this without redefining the abstraction.

- Start with a small fixed set of habitats and only generalize further if later work truly needs it.

Design principle:
- A habitat is a surface or zone where biofilm can colonize, decomposition can occur, or redox conditions can differ from the bulk water column.
- Each habitat knows: its colonizable area (cm²), its flow exposure (normalized 0-1), its oxygen exposure (normalized 0-1), and optionally its light exposure.
- Biomass pools (nitrifiers, decomposers, periphyton) will later be indexed by habitat. For now, the registry just provides the geometry and modifiers.
